paper_title: Searching for an oscillating massive scalar field as a dark matter candidate using atomic hyperfine frequency comparisons
notes: Limits extracted from Fig. 3 (bottom panel, red 95% CL curve) on upper bounds of d_e + 0.043(d_m̂ - d_g) versus scalar field mass m_φ. This combination arises from the Rb/Cs hyperfine frequency ratio sensitivity to variations in fine structure constant (d_e, Damour-Donoghue coupling) and QCD mass scale / quark mass terms. Most stringent limit: d_e + 0.043(d_m̂ - d_g) < 3.8×10^-9 at m_φ = 1.4×10^-23 eV (Eq. 8, Fig. 3). When assuming pure electromagnetic coupling (d_m̂ - d_g = 0), these limits directly constrain d_e and improve prior Dy spectroscopy constraints (Ref. 2) by >order of magnitude. Measurement spans 2009-2016 using FO2 dual Rb/133Cs fountain at LNE-SYRTE. No signal detected; limits set at 95% confidence level via Bayesian analysis of harmonic amplitude spectrum.
